guarantees.claim: unused_seed_data is continuously assigned the value of entropy_seed_data.
unused_seed_update is continuously assigned the value of entropy_seed_update.
unused_refresh_period is continuously assigned the XOR reduction of the concatenation {wait_timer_limit, wait_timer_prescaler}.
unused_entropy_refresh_req is continuously assigned the value of entropy_refresh_req.

uncertain_points.claim: entropy_seed_data and entropy_seed_update are routed to unused outputs only, possibly discarding entropy seeds required for KMAC key derivation or internal reseeding.
uncertain_points.cond: when entropy source provides seed data and update pulse, these values have no effect inside kmac
uncertain_points.risk: KMAC may operate with weak or stale secret material, compromising MAC integrity or key confidentiality.

uncertain_points.claim: entropy_refresh_req is connected only to an unused output; the module may ignore an explicit entropy refresh request.
uncertain_points.risk: entropy refresh does not occur, potentially leaving the PRNG or key state stale and vulnerable to side‑channel or prediction attacks.

uncertain_points.claim: wait_timer_limit and wait_timer_prescaler only appear in an XOR reduction tied to an unused output; their values do not affect any internal timer or FSM.
uncertain_points.cond: always, as the reduction result drives only an unused port
uncertain_points.risk: intended wait‑timer configuration may be ignored, causing incorrect inter‑message delays or timing‑side‑channel exposure.
